title: One In, One Out? Elastic Collision Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A marble hits a still marble and stops dead. A ball hits a wall and bounces straight back. And on Aarav's desk toy, swing one steel ball in and exactly one flies out, swing two and two fly out. Why never one ball, twice as fast? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn the elastic collision in one dimension, where both momentum and kinetic energy are kept.

On a live motion notebook two steel balls collide in three runs (equal masses, heavy into light, light into heavy) while the readout and a kinetic energy vs time graph track every joule. A slow-mo replay freezes the biggest squash, where the energy hides for a moment and then comes back. We derive v1 = (m1 - m2)u1/(m1 + m2) and v2 = 2m1u1/(m1 + m2) step by step, solve the desk toy puzzle link by link, compare the heavy and light limits side by side, and work a full example. Then the exam trap (elastic bodies do not always swap velocities), an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
